detail.title: Robustness and Redundancy in Quantum and Classical Records
detail.summary: Robustness in physical records is achieved when system pointer states are redundantly encoded into environmental degrees of freedom, enabling independent observers to reach consensus. This process, formalizable through Spectrum Broadcast Structures (SBS) and quantum Darwinism, effectively 'broadcasts' information. Furthermore, thermodynamic constraints, specifically the energy cost of erasing information (Landauer's principle), bound the long-term stability of these records in both classical and quantum substrates.
detail.reason: Notebook revision required to integrate thermodynamic constraints on record stability with existing redundancy frameworks.

detail.title: Mechanisms of Objectivity: Quantum Darwinism and Redundancy
detail.summary: Robustness in quantum records emerges through the redundant broadcasting of system states into environmental degrees of freedom. Multiple independent observers can retrieve consistent information about the system's pointer states. However, this process is critically sensitive to noise and scrambling dynamics, which can degrade the fidelity of the redundantly encoded information.
detail.reason: The notebook has been revised to incorporate new source material regarding noise thresholds and experimental control in atomic systems, strengthening the discussion of robustness.

detail.title: Mechanisms of Objectivity: Quantum Darwinism and Redundancy
detail.summary: Robustness in quantum records emerges through the redundant broadcasting of system states into environmental degrees of freedom. Multiple independent observers can retrieve consistent information (pointer states) because these states are 'einselected' and amplified by the environment, creating a classical-like objective record. Information scrambling, however, delocalizes information, potentially competing with the formation of these local redundant records.
detail.reason: Synthesized recent peer-reviewed sources to clarify the interplay between redundancy and scrambling in objective record formation.

detail.title: Mechanisms of Objectivity: Quantum Darwinism and Redundancy
detail.summary: Robustness in quantum records arises from the redundancy of information stored in the environment. Quantum Darwinism framework posits that multiple observers can retrieve the same information by measuring distinct fragments of the environment, provided those fragments decohere into preferred pointer states.
detail.reason: Revision required to solidify the link between redundancy and observer consensus using established peer literature.
